title: Factory Safety Directives & ISO Standards: Modals of Obligation
description: Apply must, have to, must not, and don't have to accurately in workshop PPE regulations, hazardous material protocols, and ISO 9001/45001 compliance.
learning_objectives: Differentiate external obligation ('have to') from speaker authority ('must')
Distinguish absolute prohibition ('must not') from absence of obligation ('don't have to')
Avoid critical Czenglish safety rule misinterpretations

questions.prompt: Under Tatra plant safety regulations, all shop floor visitors _____ steel-toe safety boots at all times.

explanations.correct: 'Have to wear' (or 'must wear') expresses mandatory institutional obligation imposed by external regulations.
explanations.wrong_A: Modal verb 'must' is followed directly by base form, never by 'to' infinitive ('must to wear' is ungrammatical).
explanations.wrong_C: 'Don't have to' means it is optional, which violates safety rules.
explanations.wrong_D: Present continuous does not express a regulatory obligation.

questions.cz_learning_point: Never add 'to' after 'must' (*must to wear* is an extremely common Czenglish slip). Use 'must wear' or 'have to wear'.

questions.prompt: You _____ touch the high-voltage battery disconnect switch on the hybrid prototype without certified insulated gloves!

explanations.wrong_A: 'Don't have to' means lack of necessity (nemusíš), meaning you can if you want—a fatal misunderstanding in high-voltage safety!
explanations.wrong_B: 'Haven't to' is an invalid English modal auxiliary.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Needn't' means lack of necessity, not strict prohibition.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'nemusíš' = 'don't have to / needn't', while 'nesmíš' = 'must not'. Confusing these two in safety contexts can cause severe accidents.

questions.prompt: Line technicians _____ manually log torque values on paper anymore, because the smart wrenches upload data via Wi-Fi automatically.

explanations.correct: 'Don't have to' expresses that the task is no longer necessary (absence of obligation).
explanations.wrong_B: 'Must not' means it is forbidden, whereas it is simply automated and unnecessary.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Should not' expresses negative moral or advisory recommendation.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'nemusí' is correctly rendered as 'don't have to' or 'don't need to'.

questions.prompt: Before dispatching the vehicle for rail shipment, the export team _____ obtain a certified phytosanitary clearance for wooden shipping cradles.

explanations.correct: 'Has to' reflects 3rd person singular agreement with 'team' expressing mandatory export law requirement.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Must to' is ungrammatical; modals take bare infinitive.
explanations.wrong_C: 'Is having' does not express modal obligation.

questions.cz_learning_point: Modals like 'must' and 'should' never take 'to' (*must to*, *should to* are incorrect).

questions.prompt: Because the assembly line suffered a breakdown yesterday, the chassis department _____ work an extra weekend shift.

explanations.correct: The past tense of modal obligation ('must / have to') is always 'had to'.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Musted' does not exist; 'must' has no past tense form.
explanations.wrong_B: Present perfect does not match the past temporal marker 'yesterday'.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Must' cannot be used for past completed obligations.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech uses past tense of 'muset' ('museli jsme'). In English, the past tense of 'must' is always 'had to'.

questions.prompt: Operators _____ operate the 50-ton overhead gantry crane unless they hold an active certification badge.

explanations.correct: 'Are not permitted to' (or 'must not') expresses formal safety prohibition without authorization.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Don't have to' would make certification optional, which is unsafe and illegal.

questions.cz_learning_point: In safety directives, 'není povoleno' is formally rendered as 'are not permitted to' or 'are strictly prohibited from'.

questions.prompt: Does the welding team _____ submit an 8D non-conformity report for minor cosmetic spatter?

explanations.correct: Questions with auxiliary 'Do / Does' require 'have to' for obligation ('Does the team have to submit...?').
explanations.wrong_A: 'Must' does not form questions with 'Does' (*Does the team must...?* is ungrammatical).
explanations.wrong_B: 'Ought' requires 'to', but is not used with 'Does'.
explanations.wrong_C: Auxiliary 'Does' already carries 3rd person '-s', so base form 'need to' or 'have to' is required.

questions.cz_learning_point: You cannot ask '*Must the team...*' in standard workplace English; always ask 'Does the team have to...?'

questions.prompt: During emergency fire drills, all workshop personnel _____ evacuate immediately via marked exit corridors.

explanations.correct: 'Must' conveys urgent, non-negotiable imperative directly from emergency safety protocols.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Can' expresses optional capability, not an emergency evacuation mandate.

questions.cz_learning_point: Emergency notices use 'must' + bare infinitive to signal non-negotiable compliance.

questions.prompt: You _____ clean the test cell floors today; the industrial sanitation contractor handles that on Friday evenings.

explanations.correct: 'Needn't' (or 'don't need to') indicates that the task is unnecessary.
explanations.wrong_A: 'Must not' implies that cleaning the floor is strictly forbidden.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Aren't' cannot stand alone before a base verb.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'nemusíš' = 'needn't' or 'don't have to'. Avoid using 'must not' when you simply mean 'it is not necessary'.

questions.prompt: According to IATF 16949 standards, all measuring equipment _____ recalibrated at least once every twelve months.

explanations.correct: 'Must be recalibrated' combines modal obligation with passive voice for equipment.

questions.cz_learning_point: In quality certifications, components require passive modal constructions ('must be inspected / must be recalibrated').
